title: Decide where the hub's per-room fanout sequence rides on the wire
description:
Catch-up (docs/design/mimi-catchup.md §4, bead mimid-1wgh.37.104) needs
the hub to put a monotonic per-room sequence on every fanout. Three
placements were weighed:

1. A new field in FanoutMessage. Plainest to read, but changes a wire
   structure other implementations already parse, and ties into the
   extension-point work of bead mimid-1wgh.55.
2. Beside the message, in the POST /notify/{roomId} envelope: a header
   or a thin wrapper.
3. In an AppDataDictionary extension, if fanout ever gains one.

DECIDED by Mark, 2026-11-22: (2), beside the message.

Why: no other implementation's parser changes, so an implementation that
does not know the sequence is unaffected; a proxy cannot strip it
without the receiver noticing its absence; and it models the number
correctly. The sequence is a property of the DELIVERY, not of the
message: the same MLSMessage fanned out to five followers is one message
at one sequence, and if it were ever re-sent the sequence would be the
thing that said so. Putting it inside FanoutMessage would imply it
describes the content, which it does not.

INVENTED, NOT FROM SPEC: protocol-07 defines no sequence on fanout at
all (that is the gap bead mimid-1wgh.37.104 exists to close), so both
the sequence and its placement are ours until the working group accepts
text.

Implemented by mimid-1wgh.37.104.1.
